title.zh: 卷一百五十九 列傳第八十四 鮑李蕭薛樊王吳鄭陸盧柳崔
title.en: Volume 159 Biographies 84: Bao, Li, Xiao, Xue, Fan, Wang, Wu, Zheng, Lu, Lu, Liu, Cui
title.raw: 卷一百五十九 列傳第八十四 鮑李蕭薛樊王吳鄭陸盧柳崔 Volume 159 Biographies 84: Bao, Li, Xiao, Xue, Fan, Wang, Wu, Zheng, Lu, Lu, Liu, Cui

sentences.zh: 鮑李蕭薛樊王吳鄭陸盧柳崔

translations.literal: Bao, Li, Xiao, Xue, Fan, Wang, Wu, Zheng, Lu, Lu, Liu, Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Bao, Li, Xiao, Xue, Fan, Wang, Wu, Zheng, Lu, Lu, Liu, and Cui.

sentences.zh: 鮑防，字子慎，襄州襄陽人。

translations.literal: Bao Fang, courtesy name Zishen, was a man of Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Fang, whose courtesy name was Zishen, came from Xiangyang in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少孤窶，強誌於學，善辭章。

translations.literal: Orphaned young and impoverished, he was strongly intent on study and skilled at literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth and poor, he threw himself into learning and proved gifted at literary writing.

sentences.zh: 及進士第，歷署節度府僚屬。

translations.literal: Upon attaining the jinshi degree, he successively served as staff in military commission offices.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he held a series of posts on regional military staffs.

sentences.zh: 入為職方員外郎。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] and became Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to court and appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Appointments.

sentences.zh: 薛兼訓帥太原，被病，代宗授防少尹、節度行軍司馬，召見，慰遣之。

translations.literal: Xue Jianxun commanded Taiyuan and fell ill; Emperor Daizong appointed Fang Junior Guardian of the Capital and Military Commissioner Acting Chief of Staff, summoned him, consoled him, and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Jianxun, who held Taiyuan, fell ill, Emperor Daizong made Fang Junior Guardian of the Capital and acting chief of staff for the circuit, received him in audience, comforted him, and dispatched him there.

sentences.zh: 俄知留後，兼太原尹、節度使。

translations.literal: Shortly he became acting military commissioner, and also held the posts of Taiyuan Intendant and Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was acting military commissioner, and also served as Taiyuan Intendant and full military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 人樂其治，詔圖形別殿。

translations.literal: The people rejoiced in his governance, and an edict ordered his portrait painted in a side hall.
translations.idiomatic: The people were pleased with his rule, and the throne ordered his likeness painted for a side hall of the palace.

sentences.zh: 入為御史大夫，歷福建、江西觀察使，召拜左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Censor-in-Chief, successively served as Regional Inspector of Fujian and Jiangxi, and was summoned and appointed Left Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to serve as Censor-in-Chief, he later governed Fujian and Jiangxi as regional inspector before being summoned back as Left Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從德宗奉天，進禮部侍郎，封東海郡公。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Dezong to Fengtian, was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, and enfeoffed as Duke of Donghai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Emperor Dezong to Fengtian, was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, and created Duke of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 貞元元年，策賢良方正，得穆質、裴復、柳公綽、歸登、崔邠、韋純、魏弘簡、熊執易等，世美防知人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenyuan, in the examination for Worthy and Upright candidates, he obtained Mu Zhi, Pei Fu, Liu Gongchuo, Gui Deng, Cui Bin, Wei Chun, Wei Hongjian, Xiong Zhiyi, and others; the age praised Fang for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 1, when he examined candidates for Worthy and Upright service, he selected Mu Zhi, Pei Fu, Liu Gongchuo, Gui Deng, Cui Bin, Wei Chun, Wei Hongjian, Xiong Zhiyi, and others, and contemporaries praised his eye for talent.

sentences.zh: 時比歲旱，策問陰陽祲沴，質對：「漢故事，免三公，卜式請烹弘羊。」

translations.literal: At the time drought had persisted for years; the examination question concerned yin-yang omens and calamities. Mu Zhi replied: "By Han precedent, the Three Excellencies were dismissed, and Bu Shi asked to boil Sang Hongyang."
translations.idiomatic: Drought had dragged on for years, and the examination theme was omens and calamities in the cosmic order. Mu Zhi answered: "Under Han precedent the Three Excellencies were removed from office, and Bu Shi offered to boil Sang Hongyang alive."

sentences.zh: 指當時輔政者。

translations.literal: —aimed at those then assisting in government.
translations.idiomatic: —a pointed attack on the men then directing the government.

sentences.zh: 右司郎中獨孤愐欲下質，防不許，曰：「使上聞所未聞，不亦善乎？」

translations.literal: Dugu Min of the Right Department wanted to lower Zhi's rank; Fang would not allow it, saying: "To let the sovereign hear what he has never heard—is that not also good?"
translations.idiomatic: Dugu Min of the Right Department wished to demote Zhi, but Fang refused, saying, "Let the emperor hear what he has never heard before—is that not a good thing?"

sentences.zh: 卒置質高第，帝見策嘉揖。

translations.literal: In the end Zhi was placed in the highest grade; when the emperor saw the answer he commended it with a bow.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Zhi was ranked at the top; when the emperor read his answer he praised it with a bow of approval.

sentences.zh: 初，防與知雜御史竇參遇，導騎不引避，參謫其仆。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Fang met Associate Censor Dou Can, the escort riders did not yield; Can demoted his servants.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Fang encountered Associate Censor Dou Can in the street, his outriders failed to give way, and Can punished his attendants.

sentences.zh: 及為相，防尹京兆，迫使致仕，授工部尚書。

translations.literal: When [Can] became Chancellor, Fang was Intendant of Jingzhao; [Can] forced him to retire and appointed him Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Once Can rose to chancellor, Fang was serving as Jingzhao intendant; Can forced him into retirement and gave him the post of Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 防咤曰：「吾與蕭昕子齒，而同昕老，坐宰相余忿邪！」

translations.literal: Fang exclaimed: "I am of the same age as Xiao Xin, yet grow old together with Xin—am I to sit idle because of a chancellor's leftover spite!"
translations.idiomatic: Fang cried out in indignation: "Xiao Xin and I are the same age, yet I am growing old alongside him—am I to be sidelined because a chancellor still bears a grudge?"

sentences.zh: 不得誌卒，年六十九，贈太子少保，謚曰宣。

translations.literal: He died without fulfilling his ambition at age sixty-nine; posthumously he was given Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous title Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine without seeing his ambitions realized; he was posthumously made Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Xuan.

sentences.zh: 防於詩尤工，有所感發，以譏切世敝，當時稱之。

translations.literal: Fang was especially skilled in poetry; stirred by experience, he used it to satirize the ills of the age, and his day praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Fang was especially accomplished in poetry; moved by what he had lived through, he used verse to skewer the failings of the times, and contemporaries acclaimed him for it.

sentences.zh: 與中書舍人謝良弼友善，時號「鮑謝」雲。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Secretariat Drafter Xie Liangbi; the age called them "Bao and Xie."
translations.idiomatic: He was close friends with Secretariat Drafter Xie Liangbi, and people of the time spoke of them as "Bao and Xie."

sentences.zh: 李自良，兗州泗水人。

translations.literal: Li Ziliang was a man of Sishui in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ziliang came from Sishui in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 天寶亂，往從兗鄆節度使能元皓。

translations.literal: When the Tianbao turmoil broke out, he went to follow Military Commissioner Neng Yuanhao of Yan-Yan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao rebellion he joined the staff of Neng Yuanhao, military commissioner of Yan and Yan.

sentences.zh: 以戰多，累授右衛率。

translations.literal: Because of many battles, he was repeatedly appointed Colonel of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His long record in combat won him repeated promotion, eventually to colonel of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 從袁傪討賊袁晁，積閥至試殿中監，事浙東薛兼訓節度府。

translations.literal: He followed Yuan Chai to suppress the rebel Yuan Chao; through accumulated merit he reached Acting Director of the Palace Domestic Service, and served in the Zhedong military commission of Xue Jianxun.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned under Yuan Chai against the rebel Yuan Chao, rose on merit to acting director of the palace domestic service, and served on Xue Jianxun's staff in Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 兼訓徙太原，又為牙將。

translations.literal: When Jianxun was transferred to Taiyuan, [Ziliang] again became a guard officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Jianxun moved to Taiyuan, Ziliang again served as an officer in his guard corps.

sentences.zh: 鮑防代總節度事，會回紇入寇，防遣大將焦伯瑜等擊之。

translations.literal: Bao Fang acted in overall charge of the military commission; when the Uyghurs invaded, Fang sent Grand Generals Jiao Boyu and others to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: While Bao Fang was acting military commissioner, the Uyghurs raided the frontier; Fang sent his senior generals Jiao Boyu and others to meet them.

sentences.zh: 自良曰：「寇遠來，難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: Ziliang said: "The enemy has come from afar; it is hard to contend with them in direct battle.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang said, "The raiders have marched a great distance; we should not try to beat them in a pitched fight.

sentences.zh: 請築二壘搤歸路，堅壁勿出，求戰不許，師老而墮，其勢易乘。」

translations.literal: I ask to build two forts to choke their return route, hold the walls and not go out, grant no battle when they seek it; when the army grows weary and slackens, their momentum will be easy to exploit."
translations.idiomatic: Build two forts to block their line of retreat, hold fast behind the walls, and refuse every challenge to fight; once their troops grow tired and careless, we can strike at an advantage."

sentences.zh: 防不聽。

translations.literal: Fang did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Fang would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 伯瑜戰百井，大敗。

translations.literal: Boyu fought at Baijing and suffered a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Boyu gave battle at Baijing and was routed.

sentences.zh: 由是知名。

translations.literal: From this he became known.
translations.idiomatic: From that time his name became known.

sentences.zh: 馬燧代防，表為軍候。

translations.literal: Ma Sui replaced Fang and memorialized [the court] to appoint [Ziliang] army adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Ma Sui succeeded Fang, he recommended Ziliang as army adjutant.

sentences.zh: 自良為人勤且有謀，燧倚信之。

translations.literal: Ziliang as a man was diligent and possessed stratagems; Sui relied on and trusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent and resourceful by nature, Ziliang won Sui's full trust.

sentences.zh: 從討田悅還，攻李懷光河中，數履鋒陷陣，功在諸將右。

translations.literal: Returning from campaigning against Tian Yue, he attacked Li Huai'guang in Hezhong; repeatedly he braved the front and broke into enemy formations, his merit ranking above the other generals.
translations.idiomatic: After the campaign against Tian Yue he helped crush Li Huai'guang in Hezhong, repeatedly leading charges into the enemy lines until his achievements outshone every other commander.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，燧來朝，德宗罷燧兵，以自良代之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan, Sui came to court; Dezong removed Sui's command and had Ziliang replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 3, when Sui came to court, Dezong stripped him of command and named Ziliang to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 自良以事燧久，不敢當，議者多其讓，乃授右龍武大將軍。

translations.literal: Ziliang, having long served Sui, did not dare accept; many in discussion praised his yielding, and [the court] then appointed him Grand General of the Right Dragon Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang had served under Sui for years and shrank from taking his place; court opinion praised his modesty, and for the moment he was made grand general of the Right Dragon Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 入謝，帝終以河東近胡，謂曰：「卿於進退寧不有禮？

translations.literal: On entering to give thanks, the emperor ultimately because Hedong was near the barbarians said: "In advancing and withdrawing, do you truly lack propriety?
translations.idiomatic: When he came in to give thanks, the emperor said at last, mindful that Hedong lay on the northern frontier: "Surely you know the proprieties of office—why hang back?

sentences.zh: 然守北門無易卿者，勉為朕行。」

translations.literal: Yet to guard the northern gate there is no one to replace you—strive to go for Us."
translations.idiomatic: Yet there is no one better suited to hold the northern gate; do this for me."

sentences.zh: 乃以檢校工部尚書充河東節度使。

translations.literal: He was then made Acting Minister of Works and Military Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 居治九年，舉不愆法，簡儉易循，民不知有軍，上下諧附。

translations.literal: In nine years of governance nothing violated the law; simplicity and thrift were easy to follow; the people did not know there was an army; superiors and subordinates were in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He governed for nine years without a breach of law, ruling with simplicity and thrift so that the people scarcely felt the presence of troops and officers and men alike were united.

sentences.zh: 卒於官，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He died in office; posthumously he was given Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 蕭昕，字中明，梁鄱陽王恢七世孫，世居河南。

translations.literal: Xiao Xin, courtesy name Zhongming, was seventh-generation descendant of Prince Hui of Poyang of Liang, his family long residing in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Xin, courtesy name Zhongming, was a seventh-generation descendant of Prince Hui of Poyang of Liang, and his family had long lived in Henan.

sentences.zh: 再中博學宏辭科，調壽安尉，累遷左補闕。

translations.literal: Twice he passed the Broad Learning and Eloquent Expression examination, was assigned as magistrate of Shou'an, and was repeatedly promoted to Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: He twice passed the Broad Learning and Eloquent Expression examination, was posted as magistrate of Shou'an, and rose step by step to Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 哥舒翰為副元帥拒安祿山，辟掌書記，翰敗，儳道走蜀。

translations.literal: Geshu Han was deputy supreme commander resisting An Lushan and recruited [Xin] as chief secretary; when Han was defeated, [Xin] took bypaths and fled to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: When Geshu Han served as deputy supreme commander against An Lushan he took Xin on as chief secretary; after Han's defeat Xin made his way by back roads into Shu.

sentences.zh: 肅宗立，奉誥冊見行在。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong was enthroned, [Xin] presented the edict and patent of investiture and was received at the mobile court.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Suzong took the throne, Xin presented the enthronement documents and was received at the mobile court.

sentences.zh: 歷中書舍人、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: He successively served as Secretariat Drafter and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as secretariat drafter and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 代宗狩陜，昕由武關從帝，擢國子祭酒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Daizong hunted in Shaan, Xin followed the emperor through Wuguan Pass and was promoted to Chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Daizong withdrew into Shaan, Xin followed him through Wuguan Pass and was promoted to chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 建請崇太學以樹教本，帝寤其言，詔群臣有籍於朝及神策六軍子弟隸業者，聽補生員。

translations.literal: He memorialized to exalt the Imperial Academy to plant the root of instruction; the emperor awoke to his words and decreed that among officials registered at court and sons and younger brothers of the Shence Six Armies enrolled in study, they might be permitted to fill student quotas.
translations.idiomatic: He urged that the Imperial Academy be elevated to anchor the foundations of learning; the emperor took his point and ordered that sons of court officials on the roster and youths of the Shence Six Armies enrolled in study might be admitted as academy students.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，持節吊回紇。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, bearing credentials he went to condole with the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era he was dispatched with imperial credentials to offer condolences to the Uyghurs.

sentences.zh: 回紇恃功，廷讓昕曰：「乃中國亂，非我無以平，奈何市馬不時歸我直？」

translations.literal: The Uyghurs relied on their merit; in court they reproached Xin, saying: "It was China in turmoil—without us there could be no pacification; why, when buying horses, do you not promptly return our price?"
translations.idiomatic: Taking credit for their service, the Uyghurs confronted Xin in open court: "China was in chaos—without us you could never have restored order—so why do you not pay promptly for the horses you buy?"

sentences.zh: 眾失色。

translations.literal: The assembly turned pale.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the embassy party blanched.

sentences.zh: 昕徐曰：「國家龕定寇難，功雖絲毫不遺賞，況鄰國乎？

translations.literal: Xin said calmly: "The state has settled the bandit calamity; though merit not a thread's breadth goes unrewarded, how much more a neighboring state?
translations.idiomatic: Xin answered calmly: "The empire has put down the rebellion; not the smallest merit goes unrewarded at home—how much less a neighboring power?

sentences.zh: 仆固懷恩，我之叛臣，爾與連禍，又引吐蕃暴我郊甸。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en was our rebel minister; you shared his misfortune, and moreover led the Tibetans to ravage our suburban fields.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en was our traitor, yet you shared his fate, and you even brought the Tibetans to ravage our borderlands.

sentences.zh: 天舍其衷，吐蕃敗北，回紇悔懼，叩顙乞和。

translations.literal: Heaven abandoned their hearts; the Tibetans were defeated in the north; the Uyghurs repented and feared, knocking their foreheads to beg peace.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven turned from them: Tibet was beaten back, the Uyghurs were filled with remorse and fear, and they knocked their foreheads on the ground begging for peace.

sentences.zh: 非天子恤舊功，則只馬不得出塞下，孰為失信者？」

translations.literal: Had the Son of Heaven not pitied old merit, then not a single horse could leave below the passes—who is the one who broke faith?"
translations.idiomatic: If the Son of Heaven had not shown mercy for past service, not one horse would have crossed the frontier—so who is it that failed to keep faith?"

sentences.zh: 回紇大慚，因厚禮昕，遣使者約和。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs were greatly ashamed, and therefore treated Xin with generous ceremony and sent envoys to conclude peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs were deeply shamed, treated Xin with great honor, and sent envoys to negotiate peace.

sentences.zh: 轉工部尚書，封晉陵侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Works and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of Works and enfeoffed as Marquis of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 德宗出奉天，昕年八十餘，步出城。

translations.literal: When Dezong went out to Fengtian, Xin was over eighty and walked out of the city.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong withdrew to Fengtian, Xin was more than eighty years old and left the capital on foot.

sentences.zh: 賊求之急，獨竄山谷間，僅至奉天。

translations.literal: The rebels sought him urgently; alone he hid among valleys and hills, barely reaching Fengtian.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels hunted him hotly; he hid alone in the hills and barely reached Fengtian alive.

sentences.zh: 遷太子少傅，爵郡公，兼禮部尚書，知貢舉。

translations.literal: He was moved to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, ennobled as Duke of a Commandery, and concurrently Minister of Rites, directing the examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent, created Duke of a commandery, and also served as Minister of Rites in charge of the civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 久之，以太子少師致仕。

translations.literal: After a long time, he retired as Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In time he retired with the title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，年九十三，贈揚州大都督，謚曰懿。

translations.literal: He died at age ninety-three; posthumously he was given Grand Governor-General of Yang Prefecture, posthumous title Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at ninety-three and was posthumously made Grand Governor-General of Yangzhou with the posthumous title Yi.

sentences.zh: 昕始薦張鎬、來瑱，在禮部擢杜黃裳、高郢、裴垍。

translations.literal: Xin at first recommended Zhang Hao and Lai Tian; while in the Ministry of Rites he advanced Du Huangchang, Gao Ying, and Pei Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Xin had early on recommended Zhang Hao and Lai Tian, and as Minister of Rites he elevated Du Huangchang, Gao Ying, and Pei Ji.

sentences.zh: 其後鎬興布衣，不數年位將相，瑱為將有威名，黃裳等繼輔政，並為名宰雲。

translations.literal: Thereafter Hao rose from commoner status; within a few years he reached general and chancellor; Tian as a general had a martial reputation; Huangchang and others successively assisted in government—all became famed ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Hao later rose from common life to general and chancellor within a few years; Tian won renown as a commander; Huangchang and the others in turn held the highest offices—all became celebrated statesmen.

sentences.zh: 薛播，河中寶鼎人。

translations.literal: Xue Bo was a man of Baoding in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Bo came from Baoding in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖文思，官中書舍人。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Wensi held office as Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wensi had served as secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 播早孤，伯母林通經史，善屬文，躬授經諸子及播兄弟，故開元、天寶間，播兄弟七人皆擢進士第，為衣冠光韙。

translations.literal: Bo was orphaned young; his father's elder brother's wife Lin was versed in the classics and histories and skilled at composition, personally teaching the classics to her sons and Bo's brothers; therefore between Kaiyuan and Tianbao, all seven Bo brothers attained the jinshi degree, a glory to the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, Bo was raised by his aunt Lin, who knew the classics and histories and wrote well; she taught her own sons and the Bo brothers herself, and during the Kaiyuan and Tianbao eras all seven brothers passed the jinshi—a shining honor for their clan.

sentences.zh: 累授殿中侍御史，遷武功、萬年令。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Attending Censor Within the Hall, and was moved to be magistrate of Wugong and Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attending censor within the hall and later served as magistrate of Wugong and Wannian.

sentences.zh: 溫敏而裕，與人交有常，李棲筠、常袞、崔祐甫並器之。

translations.literal: Warm, keen, and generous, in dealings with others he was constant; Li Qiyun, Chang Gun, and Cui Youfu all valued him.
translations.idiomatic: Warm, quick-witted, and generous, he was steady in friendship; Li Qiyun, Chang Gun, and Cui Youfu all held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 祐甫輔政，拜中書舍人，出為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: When Youfu assisted in government, [Bo] was appointed Secretariat Drafter and went out as Prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Youfu came to power, Bo was made secretariat drafter and then sent out as prefect of Ru.

sentences.zh: 坐小累，貶泉州，再遷至河南尹。

translations.literal: Because of a minor entanglement he was demoted to Quan Prefecture, then was again transferred up to Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: A minor offense sent him down to Quanzhou; he was later promoted again to intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 以禮部侍郎卒，贈本曹尚書。

translations.literal: He died as Vice Minister of Rites; posthumously he was given Minister of his former bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He died while Vice Minister of Rites and was posthumously made minister of that same department.

sentences.zh: 子公達，擢進士第。

translations.literal: His son Gongda attained the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gongda passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 佐鳳翔軍。

translations.literal: He assisted the Fengxiang army.
translations.idiomatic: He served on the staff of the Fengxiang army.

sentences.zh: 會帥不文，嘗集射，設的高數十尺，令曰：「中者酬錦與金。」

translations.literal: It happened that the commander was uncultured; once he gathered an archery meet, set the target several tens of feet high, and ordered: "Whoever hits it shall be rewarded with brocade and gold."
translations.idiomatic: The commander was a coarse man; once he called an archery contest, set the target dozens of feet high, and announced, "Whoever hits it wins brocade and gold."

sentences.zh: 一軍莫能中。

translations.literal: The whole army could not hit it.
translations.idiomatic: No man in the army could hit it.

sentences.zh: 公達執弓矢揖曰：「請為公歡。」

translations.literal: Gongda took bow and arrows, bowed, and said: "Allow me to make merry for you, sir."
translations.idiomatic: Gongda took up bow and arrows, bowed, and said, "Let me entertain you, sir."

sentences.zh: 射三發連中，眾大呼笑。

translations.literal: He shot three arrows in succession and hit; the crowd shouted and laughed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He loosed three arrows in a row and hit every time; the men roared with laughter and delight.

sentences.zh: 帥不喜，乃自免去。

translations.literal: The commander was displeased, and [Gongda] thereupon resigned of his own accord.
translations.idiomatic: The commander took offense, and Gongda resigned on his own.

sentences.zh: 復佐河陽軍。

translations.literal: Again he assisted the Heyang army.
translations.idiomatic: He then served on the staff of the Heyang army.

sentences.zh: 以國子助教居東都卒。

translations.literal: As Assistant Instructor of the Directorate of Education residing in the Eastern Capital, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Eastern Capital while serving as assistant instructor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 樊澤，字安時，河中人。

translations.literal: Fan Ze, courtesy name Anshi, was a man of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ze, whose courtesy name was Anshi, came from Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 少孤，依外家客河朔。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he relied on his mother's family and sojourned in Heshuo.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he lived with his mother's kin as a guest in the Heshuo region.

sentences.zh: 相衛節度使薛嵩表為堯山令。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Xue Song of Xiang-Wei memorialized [Ze] as magistrate of Yaoshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Song, military commissioner of Xiang and Wei, recommended him as magistrate of Yaoshan.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正，次潼關，雨淖，困不能前。

translations.literal: He was nominated Worthy and Upright; stopping at Tong Pass, rain and mud mired him so he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated for Worthy and Upright service, he halted at Tong Pass in rain and mud and could go no farther.

sentences.zh: 有熊執易者，同舍逆旅，哀之，輟所乘馬，傾褚以濟，自罷所舉。

translations.literal: There was Xiong Zhiyi, lodging at the same inn; pitying him, [Xiong] gave up the horse he rode, emptied his purse to help him, and himself withdrew his candidacy.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Zhiyi was staying at the same inn; moved by Ze's plight, he gave up his own mount, poured out his purse to help him on, and withdrew his own candidacy.

sentences.zh: 是歲，澤上第，楊炎善之，擢左補闕。

translations.literal: That year Ze placed in the top grade; Yang Yan favored him and promoted him to Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: That year Ze took first place; Yang Yan took a liking to him and had him appointed Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 澤有武力，喜兵法，議者謂有將帥器。

translations.literal: Ze had martial prowess and delighted in military methods; discussants said he possessed the makings of a commander.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was physically powerful and loved the art of war; observers said he had the makings of a field commander.

sentences.zh: 嘗召對延英，德宗嘆其論兵「與我意合」。

translations.literal: Once summoned to audience in the Yanying Hall, Dezong exclaimed of his discussion of warfare that it "accords with my intent."
translations.idiomatic: Once called to audience in the Yanying Hall, Dezong declared that Ze's views on warfare "match my own thinking exactly."

sentences.zh: 累遷山南東道司馬，就拜節度使。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Military Commissioner Aide of Shannan East Circuit, and was then directly appointed Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to military commissioner aide of Shannan East Circuit and was then appointed military commissioner on the spot.

sentences.zh: 每射獵，諸將憚其材武。

translations.literal: Whenever he went shooting and hunting, the generals feared his martial talent.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he went out hunting, his generals stood in awe of his strength and skill.

sentences.zh: 數與李希烈確，禽票將張嘉瑜、杜文朝、梁悛之等，賊氣沮縮，遂取唐、隨二州。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he clashed with Li Xilie, captured the marked generals Zhang Jiayu, Du Wenchao, Liang Junzhi, and others; the rebels' spirit shrank, and he then took the two prefectures Tang and Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Li Xilie again and again, captured enemy generals such as Zhang Jiayu, Du Wenchao, and Liang Junzhi, broke the rebels' morale, and seized Tang and Sui.

sentences.zh: 貞元三年，為荊南節度使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenyuan, he became Military Commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 3 he was made military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 會山南東道嗣曹王臯卒，軍亂，剽居人。

translations.literal: It happened that in Shannan East Circuit the Prince of Cao Li Gao died; the army mutinied and plundered the inhabitants.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Gao, Prince of Cao, died in Shannan East Circuit, the troops mutinied and looted the townspeople.

sentences.zh: 以澤威惠著襄、漢間，復徙山南東道，加檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: Because Ze's authority and kindness were renowned between Xiang and Han, he was again transferred to Shannan East Circuit and given Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Because his authority and kindness were well known between Xiangyang and Hanzhong, he was moved back to Shannan East Circuit and made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 十四年卒，年五十七，贈司空，謚曰成。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died at age fifty-seven; posthumously he was given Minister of Works, posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year of his commission at fifty-seven and was posthumously made Minister of Works with the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 訃至，帝為撤宴廢朝。

translations.literal: When the death notice arrived, the emperor for his sake canceled a banquet and suspended court.
translations.idiomatic: When word of his death reached the capital, the emperor canceled a banquet and suspended court in mourning.

sentences.zh: 子宗師，字紹述。

translations.literal: His son Zongshi, courtesy name Shaoshu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongshi, whose courtesy name was Shaoshu.

sentences.zh: 始為國子主簿，元和三年，擢軍謀宏遠科，授著作佐郎。

translations.literal: At first he was Registrar of the Directorate of Education; in the third year of Yuanhe he was selected in the Broad Military Strategy examination and appointed Assistant Editor in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: He began as registrar of the Directorate of Education; in Yuanhe 3 he passed the Broad Military Strategy examination and was appointed assistant editor in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 歷金部郎中、綿州刺史。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director of the Bureau of Revenue and Prefect of Mian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the Bureau of Revenue and then as prefect of Mian.

sentences.zh: 徙絳州，治有跡。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jiang Prefecture; his governance left traces [of achievement].
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Jiang Prefecture, he left a clear record of effective rule.

sentences.zh: 進諫議大夫，未拜卒。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Remonstrating Grand Master but died before assuming the post.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Remonstrating Grand Master, he died before he could take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 始，宗師家饒於財，悉散施姻舊賓客，妻子告不給，宗師笑不答。

translations.literal: At first Zongshi's family was rich in wealth; he gave it all away to kin, old friends, and guests; his wife and children complained they had nothing, and Zongshi laughed and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Early on his family was wealthy, but he gave everything away to relatives, old friends, and guests; when his wife and children said they had nothing left, he only laughed and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 然力學多通解，著《春秋傳》、《魁紀公》、《樊子》凡百餘篇，別集尚多。

translations.literal: Yet he studied hard and was broadly versed, authoring the Spring and Autumn Commentary, Duke Kuiji, Master Fan, and more than a hundred pieces in all; separate collections were still numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he studied tirelessly and mastered many subjects, writing more than a hundred works including a Spring and Autumn commentary, Duke Kuiji, and Master Fan, with many pieces still in separate collections.

sentences.zh: 韓愈稱宗師論議平正有經據，嘗薦其材雲。

translations.literal: Han Yu praised Zongshi's discourse as even and correct with canonical grounding, and once recommended his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu said Zongshi's arguments were fair, well grounded in the classics, and once recommended him for his ability.

sentences.zh: 王緯，字文卿，并州太原人。

translations.literal: Wang Wei, courtesy name Wenqing, was a man of Taiyuan in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, whose courtesy name was Wenqing, came from Taiyuan in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父之鹹，為長安尉，與弟之賁、之奐皆有文。

translations.literal: His father Zhixian was magistrate of Chang'an; with his younger brothers Zhiben and Zhihuan he all had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhixian had been magistrate of Chang'an, and he and his younger brothers Zhiben and Zhihuan were all known for their writing.

sentences.zh: 緯舉明經，以書判入等，歷長安尉。

translations.literal: Wei passed the Mingjing examination, entered the upper grade in document judgment, and served as magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Wei passed the Mingjing examination, ranked in the top tier of the document-judgment test, and served as magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 大歷中，與李泌俱為路嗣恭江西觀察判官。

translations.literal: In the Dali era, he and Li Mi together were administrative aides to Lu Sigong, Regional Inspector of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Dali era he and Li Mi both served as aides to Lu Sigong, regional inspector of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 泌見惡於元載，嗣恭希意欲殺之，緯護解，僅免。

translations.literal: Mi was hated by Yuan Zai; Sigong, to curry favor, wished to kill him; Wei protected and explained, and [Mi] barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Mi had earned Yuan Zai's enmity; Sigong, eager to please Zai, meant to kill him, but Wei shielded and pleaded for him until Mi barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 泌執政，奏於己有私恩，德宗許為泌報，故進緯給事中。

translations.literal: When Mi held power, he memorialized that he owed Wei a private debt of gratitude; Dezong agreed to repay Mi and therefore advanced Wei to Attendant Within the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Once Mi came to power he reported a personal debt to Wei; Dezong agreed to repay Mi by promoting Wei to Attendant Within the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 浙西觀察使缺，泌擬緯，帝曰：「是朕為君報德者乎？

translations.literal: The post of Regional Inspector of Zhexi was vacant; Mi proposed Wei; the emperor said: "Is this how We repay your debt of gratitude?
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhexi regional inspectorship fell vacant, Mi nominated Wei; the emperor asked, "Is this how I repay your favor—by sending him away?

sentences.zh: 黃門要地，獨不留議事耶？」

translations.literal: A crucial post within the Yellow Gate—and you alone would not keep him for deliberation?"
translations.idiomatic: A key post at court—and you would not keep him here to advise me?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「浙西賦入尤劇，緯清而忠，能惠養民，故請遣之。」

translations.literal: [Mi] replied: "Zhexi's tax intake is especially heavy; Wei is pure and loyal and can kindly nurture the people—therefore I ask to send him."
translations.idiomatic: Mi answered, "Zhexi's revenues are especially heavy; Wei is upright and loyal and can govern the people with kindness—that is why I ask to send him there."

sentences.zh: 制可。

translations.literal: The decree was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was approved.

sentences.zh: 初，州縣有韓滉時罷錢未入者十八萬緡，府史請裒為進奉，緯上疏願蠲以紓民，詔聽之。

translations.literal: At first among prefectures and counties there were 180,000 strings of suspended payments from Han Huang's time still uncollected; the prefectural clerks asked to gather them as tribute; Wei memorialized asking to remit them to relieve the people, and an edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: At first the prefectures still owed 180,000 strings in suspended levies dating from Han Huang's time; clerks wanted to collect them as tribute, but Wei memorialized for remission to ease the people, and the throne agreed.

sentences.zh: 貞元十年，加御史大夫兼諸道鹽鐵轉運使。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenyuan he was given Censor-in-Chief and concurrently Commissioner for Salt and Iron Transport on All Circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyuan 10 he was made Censor-in-Chief and also commissioner for salt and iron transport on all circuits.

sentences.zh: 裴延齡以諸道負錢四百萬緡獻為羨錢，以圖寵，緯奏「此諸州經費」，大忤延齡意，改檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: Pei Yanling presented 4,000,000 strings of debts owed by the circuits as surplus funds to win favor; Wei memorialized that "these are the operating expenses of the prefectures," greatly offending Yanling's intent, and was changed to Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yanling reported four million strings of circuit debts as surplus revenue to win favor; Wei protested that these were ordinary prefectural funds, deeply angering Yanling, and was transferred to acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-one; posthumously he was given Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one and was posthumously made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 緯居官以清白稱，然好用刻深吏督察其下，條約苛碎，人不聊雲。

translations.literal: Wei in office was known for integrity, yet he liked to use harsh, exacting clerks to supervise subordinates; regulations were severe and minute, and people had no peace.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was known for integrity in office, yet he relied on harsh overseers and petty regulations so exacting that his subordinates could find no rest.

sentences.zh: 吳湊，章敬皇后弟也。

translations.literal: Wu Cou was younger brother to Empress Zhangjing.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cou was the younger brother of Empress Zhangjing.

sentences.zh: 由布衣與兄漵一日賜官封皆等，而湊畏太盛，乞解太子詹事，換檢校賓客兼家令。

translations.literal: From commoner status he and his elder brother Su on a single day received equal offices and enfeoffments; Cou feared excess grandeur, begged to resign as Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and exchanged [the post] for Acting Guest and concurrent Director of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Raised overnight from common life, he and his elder brother Su received equal offices and titles in a single day; fearing too much favor, Cou asked to step down as Mentor of the Heir Apparent and take the lesser posts of acting guest and director of the heir's household.

sentences.zh: 進累左金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was advanced repeatedly to Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose step by step to grand general of the Left Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 湊才敏銳，而謙畏自將，帝數顧訪，尤見委信。

translations.literal: Cou was talented, keen, and self-restrained in humility; the emperor repeatedly turned to consult him and especially entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: Quick-witted yet self-effacing, Cou was repeatedly consulted by the emperor and enjoyed his special trust.

sentences.zh: 是時，令狐彰、田神功等繼沒，其下乘喪挾兵，輒偃蹇搖亂。

translations.literal: At this time Linghu Zhang, Tian Shenggong, and others died in succession; their subordinates, seizing the mourning and brandishing arms, repeatedly grew arrogant and stirred disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Zhang, Tian Shenggong, and others had lately died in succession, and their subordinates used the funerals as pretexts to seize arms and stir trouble.

sentences.zh: 湊持節至汴、滑，委悉慰說，裁所欲為奏，各盡其情，亦度朝廷可行者，故軍中附。

translations.literal: Cou, bearing credentials, went to Bian and Hua, exhaustively comforting and persuading; he trimmed what they wished to memorialize, each fully expressing his situation, and also gauged what the court could carry out—therefore the armies attached to him.
translations.idiomatic: Bearing imperial credentials, Cou went to Bian and Hua, heard every grievance, shaped their petitions into what the court could accept, and won the armies' loyalty.

sentences.zh: 帝才其為，重之。

translations.literal: The emperor admired his achievement and valued him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his work and held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 元載當國久，愎狀日肆，帝陰欲誅，未發也，顧左右無可與計，即召湊圖之。

translations.literal: Yuan Zai had long held the state; his obstinacy daily grew unrestrained; the emperor secretly wished to execute him but had not yet moved; looking about, he had none with whom to plan, and immediately summoned Cou to plot it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zai had dominated the government for years and grew more arrogant by the day; the emperor meant to kill him but had no confidant—until he called Cou in to plan the move.

sentences.zh: 俄而收載賜死。

translations.literal: Shortly Zai was arrested and granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zai was arrested and ordered to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 於是王縉、楊炎、王昂、韓會、包佶等皆當坐，湊建言：「法有首從，從不應死，一用極刑，虧德傷仁。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Jin, Yang Yan, Wang Ang, Han Hui, Bao Ji, and others all should be punished; Cou proposed: "The law distinguishes principals and followers; followers should not die—if extreme punishment is applied everywhere, virtue is impaired and benevolence is harmed."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jin, Yang Yan, Wang Ang, Han Hui, Bao Ji, and others all faced punishment; Cou argued, "The law distinguishes leaders from followers—followers should not die. Mass executions would stain the throne's virtue and harm its humanity."

sentences.zh: 縉等繇是得減死。

translations.literal: Jin and the others thereby had capital punishment reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to this, Jin and the others escaped death.

sentences.zh: 丁後母喪解職。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his stepmother and left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his stepmother.

sentences.zh: 既除，拜右衛將軍。

translations.literal: When the mourning ended, he was appointed General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he was appointed general of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 德宗初，出為福建觀察使，政勤清，美譽四騰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dezong's reign he went out as Regional Inspector of Fujian; his government was diligent and pure, and fine reputation spread in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dezong's reign he was sent out as regional inspector of Fujian, where his diligent, upright rule won praise everywhere.

sentences.zh: 與宰相竇參有憾，參數加短毀，又言湊風痹不良趨走，帝召還，驗其疾，非是，繇是不直參。

translations.literal: He had a grudge with Chancellor Dou Can; Can repeatedly slandered him, also saying Cou's wind ailment made him unfit to hurry on foot; the emperor recalled him and examined his illness—it was not so—and from this the emperor did not approve Can.
translations.idiomatic: He feuded with Chancellor Dou Can, who repeatedly slandered him and claimed Cou's rheumatism kept him from walking properly; recalled and examined, Cou proved healthy, and the emperor thereafter distrusted Can.

sentences.zh: 擢湊陜虢觀察使，代李翼。

translations.literal: Cou was promoted to Regional Inspector of Shan-Guo, replacing Li Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Cou was promoted to regional inspector of Shan-Guo, replacing Li Yi.

sentences.zh: 翼，參黨也。

translations.literal: Yi was of Can's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Yi belonged to Can's faction.

sentences.zh: 宣武劉玄佐死，以湊檢校兵部尚書領節度使馳代。

translations.literal: When Liu Xuanzuo of Xuanwu died, Cou was made Acting Minister of War to head the military commission and rushed to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Xuanzuo of Xuanwu died, Cou was made acting Minister of War and military commissioner and hurried to take command.

sentences.zh: 未至，汴軍亂，立玄佐子士寧。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, the Bian army mutinied and enthroned Xuanzuo's son Shining.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived the Bian army mutinied and installed Xuanzuo's son Shining.

sentences.zh: 帝欲遣兵內湊，而參請授士寧以沮湊，還為右金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to send troops to install Cou, but Can asked to grant Shining [the post] to thwart Cou; [Cou] returned as Grand General of the Right Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor meant to send troops to install Cou, but Can secured the appointment for Shining to block him; Cou returned as grand general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 貞元十四年夏，大旱，谷貴，人流亡，帝以過京兆尹韓臯，罷之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourteenth year of Zhenyuan there was great drought; grain was costly and people fled; the emperor blamed Jingzhao Intendant Han Gao and removed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of Zhenyuan 14 a severe drought drove up grain prices and sent refugees streaming away; the emperor blamed Jingzhao intendant Han Gao and dismissed him.

sentences.zh: 即召湊代臯，已謝，督視事，明日詔乃下。

translations.literal: He immediately summoned Cou to replace Gao; [Cou] had already thanked [the emperor] and was overseeing affairs when the edict came down the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Cou was summoned at once to replace Gao; he had already thanked the emperor and taken up duties before the formal edict arrived the next day.

sentences.zh: 湊為人強力劬儉，瞿瞿未嘗擾民，上下愛向。

translations.literal: Cou as a man was forceful, industrious, and frugal; watchful, he never disturbed the people; superiors and subordinates loved and turned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Forceful, industrious, and frugal, Cou was vigilant in office and never harassed the people; officials and commoners alike admired him.

sentences.zh: 京師苦宮市強估取物，而有司附媚中官，率阿從無敢爭。

translations.literal: The capital suffered from the palace market's forced valuation and seizure of goods; the responsible offices fawned on eunuchs and generally followed along, none daring to contend.
translations.idiomatic: The capital groaned under the palace market's forced purchases at inflated prices; officials curried favor with eunuchs and none dared object.

sentences.zh: 湊見便殿，因言：「中人所市，不便宵民，徒紛紛流議。

translations.literal: Cou saw [the emperor] in the side hall and thereupon said: "When eunuchs buy in the market, it is not convenient for the night people; it only stirs widespread talk.
translations.idiomatic: In audience at the side hall Cou said, "Eunuch buyers in the market harm ordinary townspeople and only breed endless complaint.

sentences.zh: 宮中所須，責臣可辦。

translations.literal: What the palace requires, charge your minister to provide.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the palace needs, your servant can supply it.

sentences.zh: 若不欲外吏與聞禁中事，宜料中官高年謹信者為宮市令，平賈和售，以息眾讙。」

translations.literal: If you do not wish outer officials to hear of inner-palace affairs, you should select among eunuchs those of advanced years who are cautious and trustworthy as palace market commissioners, with fair price and harmonious sale, to quiet popular uproar."
translations.idiomatic: If you prefer that outside officials not meddle in palace affairs, appoint older, trustworthy eunuchs as market commissioners to buy at fair prices and quiet the uproar."

sentences.zh: 又言：「掌閑、廣騎、飛龍、內園、芙蓉園、禁兵諸司雜供役手，資課太繁，宜有蠲省。」

translations.literal: He also said: "For the offices of Handlers of Leisure, Broad Cavalry, Flying Dragon, Inner Park, Hibiscus Park, and the various corvée laborers of the forbidden armies, the levies in kind are too numerous and should be reduced."
translations.idiomatic: He also urged cuts in the heavy corvée levies on the palace parks, cavalry offices, and guard units."

sentences.zh: 帝輒順可。

translations.literal: The emperor always assented.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved each proposal.

sentences.zh: 初，府中易湊貴戚子，不便簿領，每有疑獄，時其將出，則遮湊取決，幸倉卒得容欺。

translations.literal: At first the prefectural staff, taking Cou lightly as a noble kinsman's son, were unskilled at ledgers; whenever there was a doubtful case, when he was about to go out they would intercept Cou for a decision, hoping in haste to get away with deception.
translations.idiomatic: At first the staff, treating Cou as a mere court favorite, kept sloppy accounts; on doubtful cases they would waylay him as he left, hoping haste would let them slip through.

sentences.zh: 湊叩鞍一視，凡指擿，盡中其弊，初無留思，眾畏服，不意湊精裁遣如此。

translations.literal: Cou, tapping the saddle, would look once; whatever he pointed out all hit their flaws; at first he gave no lingering thought; the crowd feared and submitted, not expecting Cou to be so precise in judgment and dispatch.
translations.idiomatic: Cou would glance once from his saddle; every point he made exposed their tricks without hesitation, and the staff, astonished at his sharp judgment, submitted in awe.

sentences.zh: 僚史非大過不榜責，召至廷，詰服原去，其下傳相訓勖，舉無稽事。

translations.literal: For subordinate officials, unless the fault was great he did not post blame; he summoned them to court, questioned them until they confessed, then released them; his subordinates passed on mutual instruction, and nothing went unregulated.
translations.idiomatic: For minor faults he did not post public punishments but summoned clerks to court, questioned them until they confessed, and let them go; under his example the staff disciplined one another until nothing was left unchecked.

sentences.zh: 文敬太子、義章公主仍薨，帝悼念，厚葬之，車土治墳，農事廢。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenhui and Princess Yizhang died in succession; the emperor mourned them, buried them lavishly, carted earth to build tombs, and farm work was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenhui and Princess Yizhang died in close succession; the emperor mourned them with lavish burials that tied up carts and labor for tomb-building until farming stopped.

sentences.zh: 湊候帝閑徐言，極爭不避。

translations.literal: Cou waited until the emperor was at leisure and spoke slowly, arguing to the utmost without avoidance.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at leisure, Cou spoke frankly and argued without holding back.

sentences.zh: 或勸論事宜簡約，不爾，為上厭苦。

translations.literal: Some urged that in discussing affairs he be brief and restrained, or else the sovereign would grow weary and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Some warned him to keep his remonstrances short or the emperor would tire of him.

sentences.zh: 湊曰：「上明睿，憂勞四海，不以愛所鐘而疲民以逞也。

translations.literal: Cou said: "The sovereign is bright and wise, laboring in care for the four seas—he would not weary the people to indulge what he loves.
translations.idiomatic: Cou replied, "The emperor is wise and cares for the realm—he would not exhaust the people to indulge his grief.

sentences.zh: 顧左右鉗噤自安耳，若反復啟寤，幸一聽之，則民受賜為不少。

translations.literal: It is only that those at his side clamp silence and secure their own ease; if one repeatedly awakens him and he fortunately listens once, the people receive no small benefit.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants only hold their tongues to stay safe; if I keep waking him and he listens even once, the people will gain greatly.

sentences.zh: 撟舌阿旨固善，有如窮民上訴，叵雲罪何？」

translations.literal: To twist the tongue and flatter the ruler's intent is indeed fine—but if poor people appeal above, how can one say it is a crime?"
translations.idiomatic: Flattery may be pleasant, but when the poor cry out for justice, who is guilty then?"

sentences.zh: 以能進兼兵部尚書。

translations.literal: For his ability he was advanced to concurrent Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: For this service he was promoted to concurrent Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 及屬病，門不內醫巫，不嘗藥，家人泣請。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, his gate did not admit physicians or shamans; he did not taste medicine; his family wept and begged.
translations.idiomatic: When illness came upon him he refused doctors and shamans at his door and would not take medicine, though his family wept and pleaded.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「吾以庸謹起田畝，位三品，顯仕四十年，年七十，尚何求？

translations.literal: He replied: "I rose from the fields through mediocre caution, reached the third rank, held prominent office forty years, and am seventy—what more is there to seek?
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "I rose from the fields through plain diligence, reached the third rank, served prominently for forty years, and am seventy—what more could I want?

sentences.zh: 自古外戚令終者可數，吾得以天年歸侍先人地下，足矣！」

translations.literal: Since antiquity consort kin with good endings can be counted; that I may return in my natural years to attend my forebears underground is enough!"
translations.idiomatic: Few imperial in-laws ever die in peace; to live out my years and join my ancestors below is blessing enough!"

sentences.zh: 帝知之，詔侍醫敦進湯劑，不獲已，一飲之。

translations.literal: The emperor learned of it and ordered attending physicians urgently to advance decoctions; unable to refuse, [Cou] drank once.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard, he ordered physicians to press medicine on him; unable to refuse further, Cou drank one dose.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰成。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-one; posthumously he was given Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one and was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 先是，街樾稀殘，有司蒔榆其空，湊曰：「榆非人所蔭玩。」

translations.literal: Earlier, street shade trees were sparse and broken; the responsible offices planted elms in the gaps; Cou said: "Elms are not what people shade themselves under for pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the street trees had thinned out, and officials planted elms in the gaps; Cou said, "Elms are not trees people care to rest under."

sentences.zh: 悉易以槐，及槐成而湊已亡，行人指樹懷之。

translations.literal: He replaced them all with locust trees; when the locusts matured Cou was already gone, and travelers pointed to the trees and cherished his memory.
translations.idiomatic: He replaced them all with locusts; by the time they matured Cou was dead, and passersby pointed to the trees in remembrance of him.

sentences.zh: 唐興，後族退居奉朝請者，猶以事失職，而湊任中外，未嘗以罪過罷，為世外戚表雲。

translations.literal: Since Tang's rise, consort kin who retired to court attendance still lost office over affairs, yet Cou served within and without and was never dismissed for fault—he was a model among imperial in-laws.
translations.idiomatic: Since the dynasty's founding, imperial in-laws in honorary posts often lost office over scandals, yet Cou served at court and in the provinces without ever being removed for misconduct—a model for his kind.

sentences.zh: 漵子士矩。

translations.literal: Su's son Shiju.
translations.idiomatic: Su's son was Shiju.

sentences.zh: 士矩文學蚤就，喜與豪英遊，故人人助為談說。

translations.literal: Shiju's literary learning matured early; he delighted in associating with bold heroes, and therefore everyone helped speak for him.
translations.idiomatic: Shiju showed early literary promise and loved the company of men of spirit, so people everywhere spoke up for him.

sentences.zh: 開成初，為江西觀察使，饗宴侈縱，一日費凡十數萬。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng he was Regional Inspector of Jiangxi; feasts and banquets were extravagant and unrestrained, costing on a single day as much as several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng era he became regional inspector of Jiangxi and threw lavish feasts that could cost hundreds of thousands in a single day.

sentences.zh: 初至，庫錢二十七萬緡，晚年才九萬，軍用單匱，無所仰。

translations.literal: When he first arrived, treasury cash was 270,000 strings; in his later years only 90,000 remained; military expenses were bare and depleted, with nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived the treasury held 270,000 strings; by the end only 90,000 remained, leaving military funds exhausted with nowhere to turn.

sentences.zh: 事聞，中外共申解，得以親議，文宗弗窮治也，貶蔡州別駕。

translations.literal: When the matter was heard, within and without all jointly pleaded explanation; because of kinship deliberation, Wenzong did not pursue it to the end and demoted him to Assistant Administrator of Cai Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the scandal broke, court and country alike pleaded for leniency on grounds of kinship; Wenzong did not press the case to the limit and demoted him to assistant administrator of Cai.

sentences.zh: 諫官執處其罪，不納。

translations.literal: Remonstrating officials insisted on punishing his crime; [the throne] did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Censors demanded sterner punishment, but the throne refused.

sentences.zh: 於是御史中丞狄兼謨建言：「陛下擢任士矩，非私也；

translations.literal: Thereupon Vice Censor-in-Chief Di Jianmo proposed: "Your Majesty's elevation of Shiju was not private favor;
translations.idiomatic: Then Vice Censor-in-Chief Di Jianmo argued, "Your Majesty appointed Shiju without favoritism;

sentences.zh: 士矩負陛下而治之，亦非私也。

translations.literal: Shiju has failed Your Majesty and should be punished—this too is not private favor.
translations.idiomatic: to punish him for failing Your Majesty would likewise not be favoritism.

sentences.zh: 請遣御史至江西即訊，使杜江淮它鎮循習意。」

translations.literal: I ask to send censors to Jiangxi at once to investigate, so as to stop the Yangtze-Huai and other circuits from following such practices in mind."
translations.idiomatic: Send censors to Jiangxi at once to investigate, lest other circuits along the Yangtze and Huai take the same lesson."

sentences.zh: 帝聽，乃流端州。

translations.literal: The emperor listened and then exiled [him] to Duan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed and exiled him to Duan.

sentences.zh: 鄭權，汴州開封人。

translations.literal: Zheng Quan was a man of Kaifeng in Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Quan came from Kaifeng in Bian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，佐涇原節度劉昌府。

translations.literal: He attained the jinshi degree and assisted in the staff of Military Commissioner Liu Chang of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he served on the staff of Liu Chang, military commissioner of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 昌被病入朝，度其軍必亂，以權寬厚容眾，檄主後務。

translations.literal: Chang fell ill and entered court; [Quan] judged the army would surely mutiny; because Quan was generous and accommodating to the masses, [Chang] issued a dispatch putting him in charge of rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang fell ill and went to court, Quan foresaw mutiny; knowing Quan was broad-minded and popular, Chang left him in charge of rear affairs by dispatch.

sentences.zh: 昌去，軍果亂，權挺身冒白刃，明諭逆順，殺首亂者，一軍畏伏。

translations.literal: When Chang left, the army indeed mutinied; Quan braved naked blades, clearly instructed rebellion and obedience, killed the chief mutineers, and the whole army feared and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang left the army did mutiny; Quan faced drawn swords, explained loyalty and treason, executed the ringleaders, and brought the troops to heel.

sentences.zh: 德宗方厭兵，藩屯校佐得士心者，皆就命之，權自試參軍拜行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Dezong was then weary of warfare; garrison officers and aides in the circuits who won soldiers' hearts were all given appointments; Quan rose from trial military adjutant to Acting Chief of Staff.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong, weary of war, promoted officers who held their men's loyalty; Quan rose from trial adjutant to acting chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 擢累河南尹，進拜山南東道節度使，徙領德棣滄景軍。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Intendant of Henan, advanced to Military Commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, and transferred to command the De-Di-Cang-Jing armies.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to intendant of Henan, then military commissioner of Shannan East Circuit, and later commanded the De, Di, Cang, and Jing forces.

sentences.zh: 時討李師道，權身將兵出屯，奏置歸化縣，綏納降附。

translations.literal: At the time campaigning against Li Shidao, Quan personally led troops out to encamp, memorialized to establish Guihua County, and pacified and received those who surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Li Shidao he led troops in the field, memorialized for the creation of Guihua County, and pacified surrendering forces.

sentences.zh: 滄州刺史李宗奭數違命，權劾奏，詔追之，宗奭以州兵留己自解。

translations.literal: Cang Prefect Li Zongyi repeatedly defied orders; Quan impeached and memorialized; an edict recalled him; Zongyi used prefectural troops to detain himself and resign on his own.
translations.idiomatic: Cang prefect Li Zongyi repeatedly defied orders; Quan impeached him and the court ordered his recall, but Zongyi used local troops to hold his post and force his own dismissal.

sentences.zh: 憲宗更以烏重胤代權，滄人懼，共逐宗奭還京師，有詔斬以徇，徙權節度邠寧。

translations.literal: Xianzong replaced Quan with Wu Chongyin; the people of Cang feared this; together they drove Zongyi back to the capital; an edict executed him as a warning; Quan was transferred to military commissioner of Bin-Ning.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong replaced Quan with Wu Chongyin; the people of Cang, alarmed, drove Zongyi back to the capital, where he was executed; Quan was transferred to Bin-Ning.

sentences.zh: 或訟宗奭為權所誣，左遷原王傅。

translations.literal: Some sued that Zongyi had been framed by Quan; [Quan] was demoted to Tutor of the Prince of Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Some claimed Zongyi had been framed; Quan was demoted to tutor of the Prince of Yuan.

sentences.zh: 改右金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to Grand General of the Right Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made grand general of the Right Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，以左散騎常侍持節為回鶻告哀使，以足疾辭，不許，肩舁就道。

translations.literal: When Muzong was enthroned, [Quan] as Left Regular Attendant bearing credentials became envoy to announce mourning to the Uyghurs; he pleaded foot ailment but was not permitted, and was carried on shoulders onto the road.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, Quan was sent as Left Regular Attendant to announce mourning to the Uyghurs; he pleaded foot trouble in vain and was carried on men's shoulders to begin the journey.

sentences.zh: 權識詣魁然，有閎辯。

translations.literal: Quan's bearing and manner were imposing; he had broad eloquence.
translations.idiomatic: Quan was imposing in presence and spoke with force and breadth.

sentences.zh: 與可汗爭曲直，持議明壯，虜禮異之。

translations.literal: He contended right and wrong with the qaghan; his held arguments were clear and strong; the barbarians treated him with special ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He argued principle with the qaghan in clear, bold terms, and the nomads treated him with unusual respect.

sentences.zh: 使還，三遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: When the mission returned, he was thrice transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted three times to Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 用度豪侈，乃結權幸求鎮守，於是檢校尚書右僕射、嶺南節度使。

translations.literal: His expenditures were lavish; he then cultivated powerful favorites to seek a frontier command, and thereby became Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Military Commissioner of Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: His spending was extravagant; he cultivated court favorites to win a frontier post and was made acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and military commissioner of Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 多裒資珍，使吏輸送，凡帝左右助力者皆有納焉，人笑之。

translations.literal: He amassed many valuables and treasures and had clerks convey them; all who aided the emperor at his side received offerings—people laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: He amassed treasures and sent clerks to deliver gifts to everyone who had the emperor's ear, and people mocked him for it.

sentences.zh: 卒於官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 陸亙，字景山，蘇州吳人。

translations.literal: Lu Gen, courtesy name Jingshan, was a man of Wu in Suzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Gen, whose courtesy name was Jingshan, came from Wu in Suzhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元和三年，策制科中第，補萬年丞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhe he passed the Policy and System examination and was appointed aide of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 3 he passed the Policy and System examination and was appointed aide of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 再遷太常博士。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 禮史孟真練容典，博士降色訪逮，史倚以倨橫。

translations.literal: Rites clerk Meng Zhen was versed in ritual regulations; the erudite lowered his color to visit and question him; the clerk relied on this and was arrogant and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Rites clerk Meng Zhen knew the ceremonial codes by heart; when the erudite came to consult him deferentially, Meng grew arrogant on the strength of it.

sentences.zh: 會將冊皇太子，草儀，真參議偃蹇，亙榜逐之，胥曹失色。

translations.literal: When the court was about to invest the crown prince and draft the ceremony protocols, Consultant Cen Zhen was arrogant and insubordinate; Geng posted a notice expelling him, and the clerks turned pale with alarm.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of investing the crown prince, while the ceremonial protocols were being drafted, Consultant Cen Zhen grew arrogant and defiant. Geng posted a public notice ordering his removal, and every clerk in the office blanched.

sentences.zh: 遷累戶部郎中、太常少卿。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue and then Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 歷兗蔡虢蘇四州刺史、浙東觀察使，徙宣歙。

translations.literal: He served successively as Prefect of Yan, Cai, Guo, and Su, and as Zhedong Observation Commissioner, and was then transferred to Xuanshe.
translations.idiomatic: He held successive appointments as prefect of Yan, Cai, Guo, and Su, served as Zhedong Observation Commissioner, and was later transferred to Xuanshe.

sentences.zh: 太和八年卒，年七十一，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Taihe he died at the age of seventy-one and was posthumously awarded the title Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the eighth year of Taihe at seventy-one, and the court posthumously honored him as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 亙文明嚴重，所到以善政稱。

translations.literal: Geng was cultured, solemn, and dignified; wherever he served he was praised for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Geng was learned, grave, and imposing, and in every post he earned a reputation for wise and effective rule.

sentences.zh: 初為兗州，對延英，具陳：「節度分兵屯屬州，刺史不能制，故易亂。」

translations.literal: When he first served as Prefect of Yan, at an audience in the Yanchi Hall he fully stated: "When military commissioners garrison troops in subordinate prefectures, the prefect cannot control them, and thus disorder easily arises.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his tenure as Prefect of Yan, he addressed the emperor in the Yanchi Hall and laid out the problem plainly: "When circuit armies are stationed in subordinate prefectures, the prefect has no authority over them—and that is why rebellion follows so easily.

sentences.zh: 帝因詔屯士得隸刺史。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon issued an edict that garrison troops could be placed under the prefects' command.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor promptly issued an edict placing garrison troops under prefectural command.

sentences.zh: 溫州瀕海，經賊亂，奪官吏半祿代民租，後相沿，更以為奸，亙還官全稟，繩贓罪，吏畏而賴之。

translations.literal: Wenzhou bordered the sea; after suffering bandit disorders, officials had seized half their salaries to pay taxes on behalf of the people, and this practice continued and became further corrupted; Geng restored full official salaries, punished embezzlement, and officials both feared and relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhou lay on the coast. After years of banditry, local officials had been forced to surrender half their salaries to cover the people's tax burden—a custom that lingered and grew ever more corrupt. Geng restored full pay, prosecuted graft, and the clerks came both to fear him and to depend on him.

sentences.zh: 盧坦，字保衡，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Lu Tan, courtesy name Baoheng, was a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Tan, styled Baoheng, came from Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 仕為河南尉。

translations.literal: He entered office as Assistant Magistrate of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as Assistant Magistrate of Henan County.

sentences.zh: 時杜黃裳為尹，召坦立堂下，曰：「某家子與惡人遊，破產，盍察之？」

translations.literal: At that time Du Huangchang was Magistrate; he summoned Tan to stand below the hall and said, "A son of a certain family associates with evil men and has ruined his estate—ought we not investigate?
translations.idiomatic: Du Huangchang was then magistrate of the capital district. He called Tan before him in the courtyard and said, "The son of a prominent family keeps company with scoundrels and has squandered his inheritance. Should we not look into it?

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「凡居官廉，雖大臣無厚畜，其能積財者必剝下以致之。

translations.literal: Tan said, "Whoever holds office with integrity, even great ministers, will not amass great wealth; those who can accumulate riches must necessarily exploit subordinates to obtain them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan replied, "An honest official, even at the highest rank, never hoards great wealth. Anyone who amasses a fortune must squeeze it from those beneath him.

sentences.zh: 如子孫善守，是天富不道之家，不若恣其不道，以歸於人。」

translations.literal: If their descendants are good at preserving it, that is a household Heaven-enriched through injustice; better to let them continue their injustice so it returns to the people.
translations.idiomatic: If the heirs are clever enough to hold on to it, that is a house the heavens have fattened by wrongdoing. Better to let them ruin themselves and return what they stole to the people."

sentences.zh: 黃裳驚其言，自是遇加厚。

translations.literal: Huangchang was astonished at his words and from then on treated him with increased favor.
translations.idiomatic: Huangchang was startled by the answer and thereafter treated Tan with marked regard.

sentences.zh: 李復為鄭滑節度使，表為判官。

translations.literal: When Li Fu became Military Commissioner of Zheng-Sliding, he recommended Tan as military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fu was appointed military commissioner of the Zheng-Sliding circuit, he named Tan his chief adjutant.

sentences.zh: 監軍薛盈珍數幹政，坦每據理拒之。

translations.literal: The army inspector Xue Yingzhen repeatedly interfered in government affairs, and Tan each time refused him on principle.
translations.idiomatic: The army inspector Xue Yingzhen meddled constantly in civil affairs, and Tan rebuffed him every time on grounds of principle.

sentences.zh: 有善笛者，大將等悅之，詣復請為重職。

translations.literal: There was a skilled flute player whom the generals favored; they went to Fu to request that he be given an important post.
translations.idiomatic: The generals had taken a liking to a talented flute player and asked Li Fu to give him a senior appointment.

sentences.zh: 坦笑曰：「大將久在軍，積勞亟遷，乃及右職。

translations.literal: Tan laughed and said, "Generals long in the army, having accumulated merit, are rapidly promoted even to high rank.
translations.idiomatic: Tan laughed and said, "You generals have served for years, earned your honors, and risen swiftly even to the highest ranks.

sentences.zh: 奈何自薄，欲與吹笛少年同列邪？」

translations.literal: How can you demean yourselves, wanting to stand in the same rank as a flute-playing youth?
translations.idiomatic: Why would you belittle yourselves by asking to share rank with a boy who plays the flute?

sentences.zh: 諸將慚，遽出就坦謝。

translations.literal: The generals were ashamed and hurried out to apologize to Tan.
translations.idiomatic: The generals flushed with shame and rushed out to apologize to Tan.

sentences.zh: 復病甚，盈珍以甲士五百內牙中，封府庫，舉軍大恐。

translations.literal: When Fu fell seriously ill, Yingzhen brought five hundred armored soldiers inside the inner gate, sealed the treasuries, and the whole army was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Fu fell gravely ill, Yingzhen marched five hundred armored troops through the inner gate, sealed the treasury, and threw the entire army into panic.

sentences.zh: 坦勸止之，軍乃安。

translations.literal: Tan persuaded him to stop, and the army then settled down.
translations.idiomatic: Tan persuaded him to stand down, and the army gradually calmed.

sentences.zh: 復卒，詔姚南仲代之。

translations.literal: When Fu died, the court ordered Yao Nanzhong to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu's death, the court appointed Yao Nanzhong to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 盈珍以南仲本書生，易之，曰：「是將材邪？」

translations.literal: Yingzhen looked down on Nanzhong as a mere scholar and underestimated him, saying, "Is this fellow even soldier material?
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen dismissed Nanzhong as a bookish man and easy prey. "Is this one even fit to command?" he said.

sentences.zh: 坦私謂人曰：「姚大夫外柔中剛，監軍若侵之，必不受。

translations.literal: Tan privately told others, "Commissioner Yao is outwardly gentle but inwardly firm; if the army inspector encroaches on him, he will not yield.
translations.idiomatic: Tan confided to others, "Commissioner Yao is soft in manner but iron at the core. If the inspector pushes him, he will not yield.

sentences.zh: 我留，恐及禍。」

translations.literal: If I remain, I fear disaster will reach me.
translations.idiomatic: If I stay, I fear I will be caught in the fallout.

sentences.zh: 乃從復喪歸東都，為壽安令。

translations.literal: He therefore followed Fu's funeral procession back to the eastern capital and served as Magistrate of Shou'an.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore escorted Fu's coffin back to the eastern capital and took up the post of magistrate of Shou'an.

sentences.zh: 盈珍果與南仲不相中，幕府多黜死者。

translations.literal: Yingzhen indeed came into conflict with Nanzhong, and many staff members in the headquarters were dismissed or put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzhen and Nanzhong clashed as Tan had foreseen, and many men in the headquarters were demoted or killed.

sentences.zh: 河南賦限已窮，縣人訴機織未就，坦詣府請申十日。

translations.literal: The tax deadline for Henan had already expired, and the county people pleaded that their weaving was not yet finished; Tan went to the prefectural office to request a ten-day extension.
translations.idiomatic: Henan's tax deadline had passed, and the people of the county pleaded that their weaving was still unfinished. Tan went to the prefecture and asked for ten more days.

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: His request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 坦諭縣人第輸，勿顧限，違之不過罰令俸爾。

translations.literal: Tan instructed the county people to pay in order of household and not worry about the deadline, saying that violating it would at most cost the magistrate his salary.
translations.idiomatic: Tan told the people to pay household by household and ignore the deadline—the worst that could happen, he said, was a fine against the magistrate's own salary.

sentences.zh: 由是知名。

translations.literal: Because of this he became well known.
translations.idiomatic: From that episode his name spread.

sentences.zh: 累為刑部郎中，兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice, concurrently serving as Supervising Censor in charge of mixed affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice and concurrently served as Supervising Censor handling general censorial business.

sentences.zh: 赤縣尉為臺所按，京兆尹密救之，帝遣中人就釋。

translations.literal: An assistant magistrate of the capital district was investigated by the censorate; the Jingzhao Governor secretly sought to save him, and the Emperor sent eunuchs to secure his release.
translations.idiomatic: When a capital-district assistant magistrate came under censorial investigation, the Jingzhao governor secretly intervened on his behalf, and the emperor dispatched eunuchs to have him freed.

sentences.zh: 坦白中丞，請中覆，中人走以聞，帝曰：「吾固宜先命有司。」

translations.literal: Tan memorialized openly, requesting a formal review of the case; the eunuchs hurried back to report, and the Emperor said, "I indeed ought first to have ordered the proper offices.
translations.idiomatic: Tan filed an open protest and demanded a proper review. The eunuchs rushed back to the palace with the news, and the emperor said, "I should have sent the matter through the proper channels first.

sentences.zh: 遂下詔，乃釋。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued, and only then was the man released.
translations.idiomatic: Only after an edict was issued was the man released.

sentences.zh: 數月遷中丞。

translations.literal: Several months later he was promoted to Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 初，諸道長吏罷還者，取本道錢為進奉，帝因赦令一切禁止，而山南節度使柳晟、浙西觀察使閻濟美格詔輸獻，坦劾奏，晟、濟美白衣待罪。

translations.literal: Earlier, when regional governors and prefects returned after leaving office, they took local funds as tribute offerings; the Emperor therefore forbade this entirely in an amnesty edict, yet the Shannan Military Commissioner Liu Sheng and the Zhexi Observation Commissioner Yan Jimei submitted tribute in violation of the edict; Tan impeached them, and Liu and Yan wore white and awaited punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, outgoing regional governors had carried home local funds as tribute. The emperor banned the practice in a general amnesty, but Shannan Military Commissioner Liu Sheng and Zhexi Observation Commissioner Yan Jimei submitted gifts anyway. Tan impeached them, and both men appeared in white to await judgment.

sentences.zh: 帝諭坦曰：「二人所獻皆家財，朕已許原，不可失信。」

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed Tan, "What these two men offered was their own household wealth; I have already agreed to pardon them—it would not do to break faith.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Tan, "Both men gave from their own purses, and I have already promised to forgive them. I cannot go back on my word.

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「所以布大信者，赦令也。

translations.literal: Tan said, "What spreads great faith is the amnesty edict.
translations.idiomatic: Tan replied, "Your Majesty's great pledge to the realm is the amnesty edict itself.

sentences.zh: 今二臣違詔，陛下奈何以小信失大信乎！」

translations.literal: Now these two ministers have violated the edict—how can Your Majesty sacrifice great faith for the sake of a small promise!
translations.idiomatic: These two ministers have defied it. How can you sacrifice the empire's trust for the sake of a private promise?

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕既受之，奈何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Since I have already accepted it, what can be done?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "But I have already accepted their gifts. What am I to do?"
