sentences.zh: 坦曰：「出歸有司，以明陛下之德。」

translations.literal: Tan said, "Return them to the proper offices to make clear Your Majesty's virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "Return the gifts to the proper offices. That will show the court's integrity."

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 李锜誅，有司將毀其祖墓，坦上疏諫止。

translations.literal: After Li Qi was executed, the proper offices were about to destroy his ancestral tombs; Tan submitted a memorial urging that this be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Qi was put to death, the authorities planned to demolish his family tombs. Tan memorialized the throne to forbid it.

sentences.zh: 裴均為僕射，將居諫議、常侍上，坦引故事及姚南仲舊比。

translations.literal: When Pei Jun was appointed Vice Director of the Left and was to rank above the Remonstrance and Regular Attendant officials, Tan cited precedent and the old comparison with Yao Nanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Jun was made Left Vice Director and was to take precedence over the remonstrance and regular attendant officials, Tan invoked precedent and the earlier case of Yao Nanzhong.

sentences.zh: 均曰：「南仲何人？」

translations.literal: Pei said, "Who is Nanzhong?
translations.idiomatic: Pei demanded, "Who is this Nanzhong?

sentences.zh: 曰：「守正而不交權幸者。」

translations.literal: Tan said, "One who upheld righteousness and would not consort with the powerful."
translations.idiomatic: Tan answered, "A man who held to principle and refused to court the powerful."

sentences.zh: 均怒，遂罷為左庶子。

translations.literal: Pei grew angry, and Tan was thereupon dismissed and made Left Subordinate Mentor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Pei flew into a rage, and Tan was stripped of his post and relegated to Left Subordinate Mentor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 數月，拜宣歙池觀察使。

translations.literal: Several months later he was appointed Xuanshe-Chi Observation Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he was appointed Observation Commissioner of Xuanshe and Chi.

sentences.zh: 初，劉辟婿蘇強坐誅。

translations.literal: Earlier, Su Qiang, the son-in-law of Liu Pi, had been executed for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Some time before, Su Qiang—son-in-law of the rebel Liu Pi—had been executed.

sentences.zh: 強兄弘，宦晉州，自免去，人莫敢用者。

translations.literal: Qiang's elder brother Hong had served in Jin Prefecture and resigned of his own accord; no one dared employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang's elder brother Hong had held office in Jin Prefecture and then resigned on his own. No one would hire him.

sentences.zh: 坦奏「弘有才行，其弟從辟時，距三千里，宜不通謀，今坐廢，非用人意」，因請署判官，帝曰：「使強不誅，尚錄其材，況彼兄耶？」

translations.literal: Tan memorialized, "Hong has talent and ability; when his brother followed Pi in rebellion, he was three thousand li away and could not have conspired with him. To punish him now by disqualifying him from office is not the intent of employing men," and therefore requested that Hong be appointed adjutant; the Emperor said, "If Qiang had not been executed, his talent would still have been recorded—how much more so his elder brother!"
translations.idiomatic: Tan wrote, "Hong has both talent and character. When his brother joined Liu Pi's rebellion, he was three thousand li away and could not have plotted with him. To ruin him by disqualification is not how men of merit should be treated," and asked to appoint him adjutant. The emperor replied, "If Qiang himself had lived, we would still have recorded his gifts—how much more his brother!"

sentences.zh: 時江淮旱，谷踴貴，或請抑其價。

translations.literal: At that time the Jiang-Huai region suffered drought, and grain prices soared; some proposed suppressing the price.
translations.idiomatic: A drought struck the Jiang-Huai region, and grain prices shot upward. Some urged the government to force prices down.

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「所部地狹，谷來他州，若直賤，谷不至矣，不如任之。」

translations.literal: Tan said, "The territory under my jurisdiction is narrow, and grain comes from other prefectures; if the price is forced down, grain will not arrive—better to let it be.
translations.idiomatic: Tan said, "My circuit is small and depends on grain from elsewhere. If we hold prices down, merchants will simply stop bringing grain. Better to leave the market alone.

sentences.zh: 既而商以米坌至，乃多貸兵食出諸市，估遂平。

translations.literal: Before long merchants brought rice in abundance; he then lent out much military grain to the markets, and prices soon stabilized.
translations.idiomatic: Soon traders were flooding in with rice. Tan released large stores of army grain onto the market, and prices settled.

sentences.zh: 再遷戶部侍郎，判度支。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Vice Minister of Revenue and concurrently placed in charge of the Directorate of Budgets.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Vice Minister of Revenue and given charge of the Directorate of Budgets.

sentences.zh: 或告泗州刺史薛謇為代北水運時，畜異馬，不以獻，事下度支。

translations.literal: Someone reported that when Xue Qian was Prefect of Sizhou and served on the northern water transport route, he had kept exceptional horses and had not presented them as tribute; the matter was referred to the Directorate of Budgets.
translations.idiomatic: An informer accused Sizhou Prefect Xue Qian of hoarding rare horses while serving on the northern water-transport route instead of presenting them to the throne. The case went to the Directorate of Budgets.

sentences.zh: 坦遣吏驗，未反，帝遲之，更遣中人劉泰昕往。

translations.literal: Tan dispatched officials to verify the report, but before they returned the Emperor grew impatient and further sent the eunuch Liu Taixin.
translations.idiomatic: Tan sent clerks to investigate, but before they returned the emperor grew restless and dispatched the eunuch Liu Taixin as well.

sentences.zh: 坦曰：「事付有司，而又遣宦官，豈有司不足信乎？」

translations.literal: Tan said, "The matter has been entrusted to the proper offices, yet eunuchs are also sent—is this not to say that the proper offices are not trustworthy?
translations.idiomatic: Tan protested, "The case belongs to the civil authorities. To send eunuchs on top of that—is Your Majesty saying the offices cannot be trusted?

sentences.zh: 三奏，帝乃止。

translations.literal: After three memorials the Emperor stopped.
translations.idiomatic: After three memorials the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 表韓重華為代北水運使，開廢田，列壁二十，益兵三千人，歲收粟二十萬石。

translations.literal: He recommended Han Chonghua as Commissioner of the Northern Water Transport Route, opened abandoned fields, established twenty fortified posts, added three thousand troops, and collected two hundred thousand shi of grain each year.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Han Chonghua as northern water-transport commissioner. Chonghua reclaimed fallow land, built twenty fortified posts, added three thousand troops, and harvested two hundred thousand shi of grain a year.

sentences.zh: 河毀西受降城，宰相李吉甫議徙天德。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River destroyed the Western Shouxiang City, Chancellor Li Jifu proposed moving the garrison to Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: When the Yellow River wrecked Western Shouxiang City, Chancellor Li Jifu proposed relocating the garrison to Tiande.

sentences.zh: 坦以為：「城當磧口，得制北狄之要，美水豐草，邊鄣所利。

translations.literal: Tan argued, "The city stands at the desert pass and holds the key to controlling the northern barbarians; its waters are fine and its pastures rich—advantages the border defenses rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Tan objected: "That city sits at the desert gate and commands the northern tribes. Its streams are sweet and its pastures thick—the very resources the frontier depends on.

sentences.zh: 若避河流，不過退徙數里，奈何徇一時省費，墮萬世策邪？

translations.literal: If one retreats before the river, it is at most a withdrawal of several li—how can one indulge a moment's savings and abandon a strategy for ten thousand generations?
translations.idiomatic: Retreating before the river would mean shifting only a few li. How can we save a little money now and throw away a plan meant to last ten thousand years?

sentences.zh: 天德故城，地壤墝瘠，北倚山，去河遠，烽候無所統接，虜騎唐突，勢不容知，是無故而蹙地二百里，故曰非便。」

translations.literal: The old city of Tiande has poor, thin soil, backs onto mountains, lies far from the river, and its beacon towers have no connecting line; enemy cavalry can raid without warning—this is to shrink the frontier by two hundred li for no reason. Therefore I say it is not advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Tiande's old site is barren and thin-soiled, pressed against the mountains and far from the river. Its beacon towers would no longer link up, and nomad horsemen could strike before word arrived. We would surrender two hundred li of territory for nothing. That is why I say the move is unwise.

sentences.zh: 城使周懷義亦以為言。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Zhou Huaiyi also argued likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Zhou Huaiyi made the same argument.

sentences.zh: 吉甫不悅，出坦為東川節度。

translations.literal: Li Jifu was displeased and sent Tan out as Military Commissioner of Dongchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jifu took offense and had Tan posted out as military commissioner of Dongchuan.

sentences.zh: 後數月，懷義憂死，燕重旰代之，遂徙天德。

translations.literal: Several months later Huaiyi died of worry; Yan Chonggan replaced him, and the garrison was moved to Tiande.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later Huaiyi died of anxiety. Yan Chonggan replaced him, and the garrison was duly moved to Tiande.

sentences.zh: 師人怨，殺重旰，覆其家。

translations.literal: The soldiers resented this; they killed Chonggan and destroyed his household.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were furious. They killed Chonggan and wiped out his family.

sentences.zh: 初，坦與宰相李絳議多協，絳藉為己助，及坦出半歲而絳罷。

translations.literal: Earlier Tan and Chancellor Li Jiang had agreed on many matters; Jiang relied on him as his support, but half a year after Tan left office Li Jiang was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Tan and Chancellor Li Jiang had often seen eye to eye, and Jiang counted on him as an ally—but half a year after Tan was sent away, Jiang too was removed.

sentences.zh: 治東川，盡蠲山澤鹽井榷率之籍。

translations.literal: In governing Dongchuan he entirely abolished the monopoly registers for salt wells in the mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: As governor of Dongchuan he abolished every salt-well monopoly register in the hills and marshes.

sentences.zh: 吳少誠之誅，詔以兵二千屯安州，坦每朔望使人問其父母妻子，視疾病醫藥，故士皆感慰，無逃還者。

translations.literal: After Wu Shaocheng was executed, an edict stationed two thousand troops at Anzhou; Tan every new moon and full moon sent men to inquire after their parents, wives, and children and to tend their illnesses and medicine, so the soldiers were moved and comforted, and none fled or deserted.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu Shaocheng's execution, two thousand troops were garrisoned at Anzhou. On every new and full moon Tan sent men to ask after their parents, wives, and children and to see to their sickness and medicine. The soldiers were deeply grateful, and not one deserted.

sentences.zh: 惟請收軍吏閏月糧助行營，為人所非。

translations.literal: Only his request to collect the intercalary month's grain ration from army officers to supply the field camps was criticized by others.
translations.idiomatic: His one controversial move was to levy the intercalary month's grain allowance from army officers to feed the field camps.

sentences.zh: 元和十二年卒，年六十九，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanhe he died at the age of sixty-nine and was posthumously awarded the title Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twelfth year of Yuanhe at sixty-nine, and the court posthumously honored him as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 舊制，官、階、勛俱三品始聽立戟，後雖轉四品官，非貶削者戟不奪。

translations.literal: Under the old regulations, one had to hold third rank in office, salary grade, and merit before being permitted to erect halberds at one's gate; later, even if one was transferred to a fourth-rank office, unless demoted one's halberds were not removed.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation, halberds could be displayed at one's gate only when office, salary grade, and merit all reached the third rank. Later, even after transfer to a fourth-rank post, the halberds were not taken away unless the holder suffered demotion.

sentences.zh: 坦為戶部侍郎時，階朝議大夫，勛護軍，以嘗任宣州刺史三品，請立戟，許之。

translations.literal: When Tan was Vice Minister of Revenue, his salary grade was Regular Grand Master of the Palace and his merit title Protector of the State; because he had once served as Prefect of Xuan at third rank, he requested halberds and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: While Tan was Vice Minister of Revenue, his salary grade stood at Regular Grand Master of the Palace and his merit title at Protector of the State—but having once served as third-rank Prefect of Xuan, he petitioned for halberds and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 時鄭餘慶淹練舊章，以為非是。

translations.literal: At that time Zheng Yuqing, thoroughly versed in old regulations, held that this was improper.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yuqing, a master of ancient precedent, declared the award improper.

sentences.zh: 為憲司劾正，詔罰一月俸，奪戟。

translations.literal: The censorate impeached and corrected the matter; an edict fined him one month's salary and removed the halberds.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate investigated and corrected the error. An edict fined Tan one month's salary and stripped him of the halberds.

sentences.zh: 自貞元以來，立戟十八家不應令，並追正之。

translations.literal: From the Zhenyuan era onward, eighteen households that had erected halberds in violation of the regulations were all investigated and corrected.
translations.idiomatic: Going back to the Zhenyuan era, eighteen families that had displayed halberds in violation of the rules were all called to account.

sentences.zh: 閻濟美者，第進士，有長者名。

translations.literal: As for Yan Jimei, he passed the jinshi examination and enjoyed a reputation as a man of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Jimei was a jinshi degree holder known as a man of upright character.

sentences.zh: 貞元末，繇婺州刺史為福建觀察使，徙浙西。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhenyuan era he went from Prefect of Wu to Fujian Observation Commissioner and was then transferred to Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Zhenyuan reign he rose from Prefect of Wu to Fujian Observation Commissioner, then transferred to Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 為治簡易，居鎮未嘗增常賦。

translations.literal: His governance was simple and easy; while holding his post he never increased the regular tax levies.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was light and straightforward. Throughout his tenure he never raised the standing tax assessments.

sentences.zh: 罷浙西也，方在道，見詔而貢獻無所還，故帝為言之。

translations.literal: When he left Zhexi he was still on the road when he saw the edict; because the tribute gifts had nothing to be returned, the Emperor therefore spoke on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When he departed Zhexi he was still on the road when the edict reached him. Because the tribute he had sent could not be returned, the emperor interceded on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 尋出華州刺史，入為秘書監，以工部尚書致仕。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was sent out as Prefect of Hua and later entered court as Director of the Secretariat; he retired as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Prefect of Hua, later recalled as Director of the Secretariat, and finally retired with the title Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 卒，謚曰溫。

translations.literal: When he died, his posthumous name was Wen.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was given the posthumous name Wen.

sentences.zh: 柳晟，河中解人。

translations.literal: Liu Sheng was a native of Jie in Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sheng came from Jie in Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 六世祖敏，仕後周為太子太保。

translations.literal: His sixth-generation ancestor Min served the Later Zhou as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: His sixth-generation ancestor Min had served the Later Zhou as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 父潭，尚和政公主，官太仆卿。

translations.literal: His father Tan married Princess Hezheng and held the office of Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tan married Princess Hezheng and served as Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 晟年十二，居父喪，為聞孝。

translations.literal: When Sheng was twelve he was in mourning for his father and became renowned for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: At twelve, while mourning his father, Liu Sheng won wide praise for his filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 代宗養宮中，使與太子諸王受學於吳大瓘並子通玄，率十日輒上所學。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong raised him in the palace and had him study together with the crown prince and the princes under Wu Daqun and his son Tongxuan, reporting what they had learned to the throne every ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong brought him up in the palace and set him to study alongside the crown prince and the imperial princes under Wu Daqun and Wu's son Tongxuan, with progress reports submitted to the throne every ten days.

sentences.zh: 既長，詔大瓘等即家教授。

translations.literal: When he had grown up, an edict ordered Daqun and the others to teach him at his home.
translations.idiomatic: Once he came of age, an edict directed Daqun and the others to continue his instruction at home.

sentences.zh: 拜檢校太常卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Acting Grand Master of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 德宗立，晟親信用事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong took the throne, Liu Sheng was personally trusted and employed in affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: When Dezong ascended the throne, Liu Sheng became a personal favorite entrusted with state affairs.

sentences.zh: 朱泚反，從帝至奉天，自請入京師說賊黨以攜沮之，帝壯其誌，得遣。

translations.literal: When Zhu Ci rebelled, he followed the Emperor to Fengtian and volunteered to enter the capital to persuade the rebel faction and sow discord among them; the Emperor admired his resolve and permitted him to go.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhu Ci rose in rebellion, Liu Sheng followed the emperor to Fengtian and offered to enter the capital to win over the rebels and break their unity. The emperor admired his courage and sent him.

sentences.zh: 泚將右將軍郭常、左將軍張光晟皆晟雅故，晟出密詔，陳禍福逆順，常奉詔受命，約自拔歸。

translations.literal: Zhu Ci's generals, the Right General Guo Chang and the Left General Zhang Guangcheng, were old acquaintances of Liu Sheng; Liu Sheng produced a secret edict and explained fortune and disaster, rebellion and loyalty; Chang accepted the edict and the commission and agreed to defect and return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Ci's right general Guo Chang and left general Zhang Guangcheng were old friends of Liu Sheng. Liu Sheng showed them a secret edict and laid out the rewards of loyalty and the ruin of treason. Chang accepted the commission and pledged to break away and come home.

sentences.zh: 要籍朱既昌告其謀，泚捕系晟及常外獄，晟夜半坎垣毀械而亡，斷發為浮屠，間歸奉天，帝見，為流涕。

translations.literal: A registry clerk, Zhu Jichang, informed on the plot; Zhu Ci arrested Liu Sheng and Chang and imprisoned them in the outer jail; at midnight Liu Sheng dug through the wall, broke his shackles, and escaped; he shaved his head and became a Buddhist monk, secretly returned to Fengtian, and when the Emperor saw him he wept.
translations.idiomatic: A registry clerk named Zhu Jichang betrayed the plot. Zhu Ci seized Liu Sheng and Chang and locked them in the outer prison. At midnight Liu Sheng tunneled through the wall, snapped his chains, and fled. He shaved his head, passed as a monk, and stole back to Fengtian. When the emperor saw him, he wept.

sentences.zh: 乘輿還京師，擢原王府長史。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he was promoted to Chief Secretary of the Prince of Yuan's household.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor returned to the capital, Liu Sheng was promoted to chief secretary of the Prince of Yuan's household.

sentences.zh: 吳通玄得罪，晟上書理其辜，其弟止曰：「天子方怒，無詒悔！」

translations.literal: When Wu Tongxuan fell afoul of the court, Liu Sheng submitted a memorial clearing him of guilt; his younger brother tried to stop him, saying, "The Son of Heaven is angry just now—do not bring regret upon yourself!
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Tongxuan ran afoul of the throne, Liu Sheng memorialized to prove his innocence. His younger brother begged him to stop: "The Son of Heaven is in a rage—you will only invite disaster!

sentences.zh: 不聽。

translations.literal: He would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: He would not be dissuaded.

sentences.zh: 凡三上書，帝意解，通玄得減死。

translations.literal: In all he submitted three memorials; the emperor's mind was eased, and Tongxuan had his death sentence reduced.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three memorials in all; the emperor relented, and Tongxuan's death sentence was commuted.

sentences.zh: 晟累遷將作少監，以護作崇陵，封河東縣子，授山南西道節度使。

translations.literal: Sheng was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Directorate of Works; because he oversaw construction of Chongling Mausoleum, he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Hedong County and appointed Military Commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director of the Directorate of Works, supervised construction of Chongling Mausoleum, was enfeoffed as Viscount of Hedong County, and appointed military commissioner of Shannan West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 府兵討劉辟還，未叩城，復詔戍梓州，軍曹怒，脅監軍謀變。

translations.literal: The circuit troops returning from campaigning against Liu Pi had not yet knocked at the city walls when another edict ordered them to garrison Zizhou; the army clerks were angry and coerced the army inspector to plot mutiny.
translations.idiomatic: Troops returning from the campaign against Liu Pi had not even reached the city when a new edict sent them to garrison Zizhou. The clerks grew furious and pressured the army inspector to mutiny.

sentences.zh: 晟聞，疾驅入勞士卒，既而問曰：「若等何為成功？」

translations.literal: When Sheng heard of it, he galloped in to comfort the soldiers; afterward he asked: "What would you accomplish?
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of it, Sheng rode in hard to address the men, then asked, "What do you think you will gain by this?

sentences.zh: 曰：「誅驕不受命者。」

translations.literal: They said: "Execute the arrogant ones who refuse orders."
translations.idiomatic: They answered, "Kill the arrogant men who refuse orders."

sentences.zh: 晟曰：「若知劉辟得罪天子而誅之，奈何復欲使後人誅若等耶？」

translations.literal: Sheng said: "You know Liu Pi offended the Son of Heaven and was executed—why then would you want later men to execute you in turn?"
translations.idiomatic: Sheng said, "You know Liu Pi defied the Son of Heaven and was put to death—do you want the same done to you afterward?"

sentences.zh: 士皆免胄拜，從所徙。

translations.literal: The soldiers all doffed their helmets and bowed, following where they were transferred.
translations.idiomatic: The men removed their helmets and bowed, then marched where they were ordered.

sentences.zh: 入為將作監。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Director of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as director of the Directorate of Works.

sentences.zh: 使回鶻，奉冊立可汗，逆謂曰：「屬聞可汗無禮自大，去信自疆。

translations.literal: Sent to the Uyghurs, he bore credentials to invest the qaghan; turning back he said: "I have heard the qaghan was rude and arrogant, casting off faith and magnifying himself.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to the Uyghurs to invest the qaghan, he said on his return, "I hear the qaghan has been rude and arrogant, abandoning good faith to puff himself up.

sentences.zh: 夫禮信不能為，何足奉中國乎？」

translations.literal: If ritual and faith cannot be maintained, how is he fit to serve China?
translations.idiomatic: If he cannot keep ritual and good faith, what right has he to deal with China?

sentences.zh: 可汗諸貴人愕然駭，皆跪伏成禮。

translations.literal: All the qaghan's nobles were startled and terrified, and all knelt prostrate in full ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan's nobles were stunned; one after another they knelt in full ceremony.

sentences.zh: 還為左金吾衛大將軍，爵為公。

translations.literal: On return he became Grand General of the Left Golden Crow Guard and was ennobled as Duke.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made grand general of the Left Golden Crow Guard and enfeoffed as duke.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十九，詔從官臨吊，贈太子少保。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-nine; an edict ordered attendant officials to attend the mourning; posthumously he was given Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-nine; the court ordered officials to attend his funeral and posthumously made him Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 晟敏於辯，下士樂施。

translations.literal: Sheng was quick in debate and delighted in bestowing gifts on inferiors.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng was sharp in debate and generous to those below him.

sentences.zh: 唯自興元入朝，貢獻不如詔，為御史中丞盧坦所劾，憲宗以其賢，置弗暴雲。

translations.literal: Only from Xingyuan entering court, his tribute offerings did not match the edict, and he was impeached by Vice Censor-in-Chief Lu Tan; Xianzong because he was worthy set it forth without publicizing it.
translations.idiomatic: After entering court from Xingyuan his tribute fell short of the edict's requirements; Lu Tan impeached him, but Xianzong, judging him a worthy man, let the matter pass without public scandal.

sentences.zh: 崔戎，字可大，玄韋從孫也。

translations.literal: Cui Rong, courtesy name Keda, was a collateral descendant of Cui Xuanwei.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Rong, whose courtesy name was Keda, was a collateral descendant of Cui Xuanwei.

sentences.zh: 舉明經，補太子校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the Mingjing examination and was appointed Proofreader of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the Mingjing examination and became a proofreader in the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 判入等，調藍田主簿。

translations.literal: In document judgment he entered the upper grade and was assigned as chief clerk of Lantian.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked in the top tier of the document-judgment test and was posted as chief clerk of Lantian.

sentences.zh: 辟淮南李庸阝府。

translations.literal: He was recruited to the Huainan staff of Li Yong.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the Huainan staff of Li Yong.

sentences.zh: 衛次公代庸阝，憲宗稱戎才，故次公倚成於職。

translations.literal: Wei Cigong replaced Yong, and Xianzong praised Rong's talent, so Cigong relied on him to complete his duties.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Cigong succeeded Li Yong, Xianzong praised Rong's ability, and Cigong leaned on him to run the command.

sentences.zh: 裴度節度太原，署參謀。

translations.literal: When Pei Du was military commissioner of Taiyuan, he appointed [Rong] military planner.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du held Taiyuan as military commissioner, he made Rong his military planner.

sentences.zh: 時王承宗以鎮叛，度請戎往諭，承宗至泣下，乃聽命。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Chengzong rebelled with his command; Du asked Rong to go persuade him; Chengzong wept on arrival and then obeyed orders.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong was in rebellion; Pei Du sent Rong to reason with him, and Chengzong wept and submitted.

sentences.zh: 入為殿中侍御史，擢累諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Attending Censor Within the Hall and was promoted in succession to Remonstrating Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he became attending censor within the hall and rose to Remonstrating Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 雲南蠻亂成都，詔戎持節劍南為宣撫使。

translations.literal: When Yunnan barbarians disturbed Chengdu, an edict ordered Rong to bear credentials in Jiannan as Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Yunnan tribesmen rioted in Chengdu, the throne sent Rong to Jiannan with imperial credentials as pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 奏罷稅外姜芋錢；

translations.literal: He memorialized to abolish the extra tax on ginger and taro beyond the regular levies;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to abolish the surtax on ginger and taro;

sentences.zh: 當賦錢者率三之，以其一準繒布，優其估以與民；

translations.literal: those owing tax payments were generally assessed at one-third, with one part reckoned in silk and cloth, the valuation made favorable to the people;
translations.idiomatic: taxpayers were generally assessed at one-third of the standard levy, with one portion payable in silk at a favorable valuation;

sentences.zh: 綏招流亡。

translations.literal: he pacified and summoned back the displaced.
translations.idiomatic: he pacified refugees and brought them home;

sentences.zh: 凡廢若置，公私莫不便之。

translations.literal: whether abolishing or establishing, public and private alike found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: and whether he abolished old abuses or introduced reforms, officials and commoners alike benefited.

sentences.zh: 還拜給事中。

translations.literal: On return he was appointed Attendant Within the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made Attendant Within the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Prefect of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 吏以故事置錢萬緡為刺史私用，戎不取。

translations.literal: The clerks by precedent set aside ten thousand strings of cash for the prefect's private use; Rong would not take it.
translations.idiomatic: By custom the clerks set aside ten thousand strings for the prefect's private use; Rong refused the money.

sentences.zh: 及去，召吏曰：「籍所置錢享軍，吾重矯激以誇後人也。」

translations.literal: When he was leaving, he summoned the clerks and said: "Register the cash set aside and use it to feast the army—I would be ashamed to make a show of false austerity to impress posterity.
translations.idiomatic: As he departed he told the clerks, "Put that money toward a feast for the troops—I will not play the hypocrite for posterity's praise.

sentences.zh: 徙兗海沂密觀察使，民擁留於道不得行，乃休傳舍，民至抱持取其靴。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Observation Commissioner of Yan-Hai-Yi-Mi; the people blocked his road and he could not proceed, so he stopped at a relay station; the people came and seized his boots.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Yan-Hai-Yi-Mi, he was stopped on the road by crowds who would not let him leave; at a relay station they seized his boots in protest.

sentences.zh: 時詔使尚在，民泣詣使，請白天子丐戎還，使許諾。

translations.literal: At the time the edict envoy was still present; the people wept and went to the envoy, asking him to report to the Son of Heaven begging Rong's return; the envoy promised.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial envoy was still on the scene; the people wept before him and begged him to ask the emperor to keep Rong. The envoy agreed to plead their case.

sentences.zh: 戎恚責其下，眾曰：「留公而天子怒，不過斬吾二三老人，則公不去矣。」

translations.literal: Rong angrily reproached his subordinates; the crowd said: "If we keep you and the Son of Heaven is angered, at most he will execute two or three of us old men—then you will not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Rong rebuked his staff, but the people said, "If keeping you angers the emperor, he can only kill a few of us old men—you still will not go.

sentences.zh: 戎夜單騎亡去，民追不及乃止。

translations.literal: Rong at night fled alone on horseback; the people could not catch him and then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: That night Rong rode off alone; the crowd could not overtake him and at last dispersed.

sentences.zh: 至兗州，鉏滅奸吏十餘輩，民大喜。

translations.literal: Reaching Yan Prefecture, he rooted out more than ten corrupt clerks; the people were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanzhou he rooted out more than ten corrupt officials, to the people's great delight.

sentences.zh: 歲餘卒，年五十五，贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: After a little more than a year he died at age fifty-five; posthumously he was given Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: A little over a year later he died at fifty-five and was posthumously made Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 子雍，字順中，由起居郎出為和州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Yong, courtesy name Shunzhong, from Attendant on the Emperor's Movements went out as Prefect of He.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yong, courtesy name Shunzhong, rose from attendant on the emperor's movements to prefect of He.

sentences.zh: 龐勛以兵劫烏江，雍不能抗，遣人持牛酒勞之，密表其狀。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun's troops seized Wujiang, Yong could not resist; he sent men with cattle and wine to comfort them and secretly memorialized the situation.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun's army seized Wujiang, Yong could not hold them off; he sent cattle and wine as a gesture of conciliation and secretly reported the situation to court.

sentences.zh: 民不知，訴諸朝，宰相路巖素不平，因是傅其罪，賜死宣州。

translations.literal: The people did not know this and appealed to court; Chancellor Lu Yan, who had long disliked him, therefore spread his guilt, and he was granted death at Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The people, unaware, petitioned the throne against him; Chancellor Lu Yan, who had long borne him a grudge, made the case worse, and Yong was ordered to take his own life at Xuanzhou.
